segments.title: Why historians collaborate selectively
segments.body: Historians enjoy working together on books and videos, but the time cost limits how often they can do it. The approximate four-to-one time comparison comes from experience making joint and solo projects. Recognition and access to university or other professional positions depend on sustaining enough output, which becomes difficult if every project is a collaboration. A two-hour Bilge Pumps episode, for example, can use time that could otherwise produce two or three solo videos on the same subjects. Enjoying collaborative work does not remove that constraint. Greater control over working circumstances can make it easier to fit joint projects around other commitments.

evidence.note: Comparison of collaboration's rewards with the time and output pressures faced by historians.

segments.summary: Joint books and videos can take about four times as long as solo work, creating a conflict between enjoyable collaboration and the output needed for career opportunities.
segments.question: Why do historians not collaborate more?
segments.answerShort: Historians already collaborate and enjoy it. Joint work takes much longer, with an approximate four-to-one time comparison here, so relying entirely on collaboration makes it difficult to sustain enough output for recognition and career opportunities.

segments.title: The hidden time cost of a Bilge Pumps episode
segments.body: For Alex Clarke, Drachinifel and Jamie Seidel of Armoured Carriers, a roughly two-hour Bilge Pumps podcast can become an eight-hour commitment. The first couple of hours go into arranging topics and assembling the research. Conversation continues before anyone remembers to press the record button. The recorded episode itself lasts roughly two hours. Afterward, the group discusses and refines the points each person made and develops ideas for the next episode. The eight-hour estimate includes that preparation and informal conversation as well as the recorded programme.

evidence.note: Preparation, recording, and follow-up discussion for The Bilge Pumps.

segments.summary: A Bilge Pumps episode shows how topic planning, joint research, recording, and follow-up discussion can turn a roughly two-hour podcast into an eight-hour commitment.

segments.title: Why historical subjects need more explanation
segments.body: For the same current-affairs subjects covered by Bilge Pumps, the solo-video estimate is up to an hour and a half of research and preparation, followed by about an hour and a half of recording with slides. Familiar current figures allow shorthand because the audience already knows who is being discussed. Donald Trump supplies that example, while a historical figure such as Philip II can require an introduction. Historical explanation therefore involves context that a current-affairs discussion can often assume. In this comparison, the time spent making one two-hour group podcast could allow two or three solo videos on the same subjects.

evidence.note: Solo-video estimates of up to ninety minutes of preparation and about ninety minutes recording with slides, familiar current figures versus historical introductions, and two or three solo videos in the time spent on one joint podcast.

segments.summary: Familiar current figures let a current-affairs video use shorthand, while historical figures such as Philip II can require an introduction. The solo-video example allows up to ninety minutes of preparation and about ninety minutes of recording.

segments.title: Working autonomy can make collaboration easier
segments.body: Clarke describes a personal change in where he lives and works that gives him more control over his time. This makes collaboration easier for him to fit around other commitments. He hopes The Bilge Pumps can return more regularly, without promising a schedule. The participants enjoy talking history together, and the time that those conversations take remains the constraint.

evidence.note: Personal control over living and working circumstances and the hope of a more regular Bilge Pumps, with time still the constraint.

segments.summary: More control over living and working circumstances raises hopes of a more regular Bilge Pumps, although the time commitment remains difficult to fit around other work.
